headline: Hormuz attacks lift WTI to a six-month high while the AI rout crushes gold under $3,900
summary: Tanker attacks in Hormuz and bets on US strikes on Iran after the midterms sent WTI up 2.1% to $104.12 and expiring Brent to $117.64, while RBOB jumped 4% into its expiry. The Nasdaq's 2.9% drop on Intel and Amazon pushed money into Treasuries, cutting the 10-year about 6bp to 4.93% for a 36bp monthly fall, but forced selling and Fed hike bets sent gold down 3.6% to near $3,875 and silver under $50. Bunds rallied on softer German inflation while French yields rose after a surprise GDP contraction, and Fitch cut France's outlook after the close.
drivers: Hormuz attacks and Iran strike fears

UKMTO reported the first limpet-mine attack on a tanker in Hormuz, Iran claimed more tankers struck mines and the Houthis claimed hits on Saudi refineries, as traders expect US strikes after the Nov 3 midterms. WTI settled +$2.12 at $104.12 and expiring Dec Brent +$2.76 at $117.64; WTI rose about 15% in October.
AI cash-burn rout drives a bond rally

Intel fell 29% and the chip index 7.2% after Amazon and Intel showed heavy AI cash burn, sending the Nasdaq down 2.9%. The 2-year fell about 6bp to 4.59% and the 10-year about 6bp to 4.93%, while ECI rose 0.8% as expected and the Chicago PMI missed at 55.3.

Oil above $100 kept December hike odds near 74%, and funds sold bullion to cover equity losses: Comex gold settled -$132 at $3,885.70, a one-year low, and silver fell about 5.7% to near $49.10. Gold lost about 6.5% in October, its worst October since 2008.

French GDP fell 0.1% in Q3 and inflation rose to 3.8%, both worse than forecast, lifting the 10-year OAT to near 4.98% and the spread over Bunds to about 165bp; Fitch moved France to a negative outlook after the close. German inflation slowed to 2.8%, pulling the Schatz down about 4bp to 3.01%.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled up $2.12 (+2.1%) at $104.12, a six-month high; expiring Dec Brent +2.4% at $117.64.
oil.why: Crude rallied as traders braced for renewed US strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterms. UKMTO reported the first limpet-mine attack on a tanker in Hormuz since the war began, the IRGC claimed several more tankers hit mines, and the Houthis said they struck Ras Tanura, Rabigh and Abqaiq. December Brent's expiry squeezed the front, while the more active January contract rose $2.63 to $113.43. WTI gained about 15% in October.
oil.outlook: Bias higher in a $100–110 range into the Nov 3 midterms and any post-election strike decision. A confirmed US strike or lost Saudi output would target the April high near $113; a credible diplomatic track would pull WTI back toward $98.
oil.watch: OPEC+ Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3, EIA stocks Nov 4 and any US move on Iran.

gas.note: Nov RBOB jumped 12.70¢ (+4.0%) to expire at $3.3120, a three-week high; AAA pump average near $4.22.
gas.why: Gasoline outpaced crude on the November contract's final day, as shorts covered into expiry and the Hormuz and Saudi refinery headlines added a product-supply premium; Houthi claims named the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries. The December contract, now the front, rose about 7¢ to near $3.16 by midday. Fundamentals are softer: EIA showed a 3.9 million barrel stock build and demand down to 8.4 million b/d, and the AAA average has fallen 5¢ in a week.
gas.outlook: With December in front, range $3.05–3.30. Weak seasonal demand caps gasoline, so it should lag crude unless Gulf refinery damage is confirmed; a close above $3.30 needs real supply loss, another stock build would test $3.05.
gas.watch: EIA stocks Nov 4, Saudi refinery reports and the post-midterm Iran decision.

gold.note: Spot fell about $145 (-3.6%) to near $3,875, a one-year low; Comex Nov settled -$132 at $3,885.70.
gold.why: Gold broke the $4,000 floor as oil above $100 hardened bets on a December Fed hike, priced near 74%, after Thursday's 3.6% PCE inflation and 3.4% GDP. The Nasdaq's 2.9% slide on Intel and Amazon then forced funds to sell bullion to cover losses, so gold fell even as the 10-year dropped 6bp and the dollar eased. Gold lost about 6.5% in October, its worst October since 2008, with heavy futures volume.
gold.outlook: Bias lower in a $3,800–3,980 range while liquidation runs. A daily close back above $4,000 would signal a washout; failure at $3,850 opens $3,800, most likely if payrolls on Nov 6 lock in a December hike.
gold.watch: ISM Nov 2, the midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

silver.note: Spot fell about $3 (-5.7%) to near $49.10, first time under $50 since November 2025; down about 18% in October.
silver.why: Silver fell nearly twice as far as gold as its industrial, high-beta profile took the brunt of the AI selloff and tech-driven deleveraging. The chip index's 7.2% drop and Intel's PC warning hit the electronics demand story, and the break of $50 triggered stop and trend-fund selling, with Comex volume heavy. Silver has now erased its whole December–January run, and the gold/silver ratio rose to about 79, its highest since December.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $46–52 range. Saxo sees room to the mid-$40s if fund liquidation continues; reclaiming $52 would show the washout is done, most likely if tech stabilises and the ratio turns back down.
silver.watch: China PMIs Oct 31, US ISM manufacturing Nov 2 and payrolls Nov 6.

us2y.note: Down about 6bp to near 4.59% after a seven-week low of 4.56%; December hike odds still about 74%.
us2y.why: The 2-year extended Thursday's rally as Intel's 29% plunge and Amazon's cash burn drove a flight into Treasuries and trimmed Fed hike bets. Data did not push back: the Q3 employment cost index rose 0.8% as expected, with wages up 3.1% a year, and the Chicago PMI fell to 55.3 against 56.1 expected. Higher oil kept a floor under the front end, and December is still priced as more likely than not.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.50–4.70%. A strong payrolls on Nov 6 or oil spike after the midterms would pull it back to 4.70%; a deeper equity rout or soft ISM could test 4.50%.
us2y.watch: ISM Nov 2, the midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

us5y.note: Down about 7bp to near 4.73%, the best-performing tenor as the belly led the rally.
us5y.why: The 5-year gained most as investors bought the part of the curve most sensitive to a shift in the Fed path, betting that the AI-driven equity drawdown and slower activity data would limit how far the Fed hikes. In-line labour costs, at 0.8% for the ECI, and a weaker Chicago PMI took away any wage-inflation scare, while month-end index buying added demand. Higher oil was the only offset.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.62–4.85%. It trades with December hike pricing; a weak ISM and more tech losses favour 4.62%, a hot payrolls or an oil spike to $110 would send it back above 4.80%.
us5y.watch: ISM Nov 2, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

us10y.note: Down about 6bp to near 4.93%, the lowest since Sept 9; down 36bp in October, the most since Dec 2023.
us10y.why: The 10-year fell for a second day as the Nasdaq's 2.9% drop, its worst since June, sent money into havens; earlier it touched 4.89% in Asia. Q3 labour costs rose 0.8% as forecast and the Chicago PMI missed, so data gave no reason to sell. Month-end index extension added demand, but WTI's jump to $104 and inflation at 3.6% kept the rally from going further, steepening the curve.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.82–5.02%. More tech losses or quiet midterms could test 4.82%; a heavier coupon schedule at the Nov 4 refunding or a hot payrolls would bring 5% back into play.
us10y.watch: The midterms Nov 3, the Nov 4 refunding and payrolls Nov 6.

us30y.note: Down about 2bp to near 5.31%, lagging the belly; down 33bp in October.
us30y.why: The long bond rallied least because the day's drivers, haven demand and Fed repricing, favour shorter maturities, while oil at six-month highs kept inflation risk priced into the long end. Investors are also cautious before Wednesday's refunding and with heavy corporate supply after big tech bond deals, so term premium held and the 5s30s curve steepened by about 5bp.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.20–5.40% with a steepening bias. A larger refunding or oil spike would lift it toward 5.40%; a deeper risk-off move could pull it to 5.20%.
us30y.watch: The Nov 4 refunding, payrolls Nov 6 and the 30-year auction in mid-November.

de2y.note: Down about 4bp to near 3.01% after German October inflation slowed to 2.8%.
de2y.why: The Schatz extended its post-ECB rally after German EU-harmonised inflation slowed to 2.8% from 3.3%, below the 3.1% forecast, with core easing to 2.1% as an October fuel-tax cut lowered pump prices. That weakened the case for a December ECB hike, even though euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in Q3, twice the expected pace. Lower Treasury yields added support, while Brent above $117 limited the move.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.92–3.10%. The euro-area flash CPI on Nov 4, expected near 3.9%, is the test: a hot print lifts it to 3.10%, a soft one opens 2.92%.
de2y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4, euro unemployment and ECB speakers.

de5y.note: Down about 1–2bp to near 3.11%, following the Schatz on softer German inflation.
de5y.why: The 5-year edged lower as the German CPI miss and a falling Treasury market trimmed ECB hike pricing. It lagged the 2-year because strong 0.4% euro-area growth and oil's jump kept investors from extending into medium maturities. Haven flows from the tech rout and French stress favoured Bunds over other euro debt.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.02–3.20%. Euro CPI on Nov 4 and US payrolls set the direction; a hot CPI would lift it toward 3.20%.
de5y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4 and US payrolls Nov 6.

de10y.note: Down about 1–2bp to near 3.32%; down about 20bp in October, its best month since February.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund drew haven money as global tech stocks fell and investors rotated out of French and Italian debt after weak French and Italian GDP. German growth beat forecasts, but its inflation slowed to 2.8%, which outweighed the data. The move was modest because Brent's jump to $117.64 kept inflation risk alive, and the curve steepened slightly as the Schatz led.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.25–3.40%. More equity losses or a soft euro CPI would test 3.25%; Brent above $120 or a hot CPI would lift it toward 3.40%.
de10y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4, the US midterms Nov 3 and the BoE Nov 5.

de30y.note: Little changed near 3.68%; the curve steepened as the short end rallied.
de30y.why: The long end held steady because the day's drivers, softer German inflation and ECB pricing, mostly move short rates, while long yields are anchored by heavy euro-area issuance, oil-driven inflation risk and global term premium. Treasuries' 30-year also lagged, limiting the spillover rally, and month-end index demand was offset by caution before next week's US refunding.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.78% with a steepening bias; a global long-end selloff around the US refunding is the main upside risk.
de30y.watch: The US refunding Nov 4, the BoE Nov 5 and German supply.

fr2y.note: Little changed near 3.66%, lagging Schatz as French inflation jumped to 3.8%.
fr2y.why: Short OATs missed the core rally because French EU-harmonised inflation rose to 3.8% in October, above the 3.6% forecast, while GDP unexpectedly shrank 0.1% in Q3. The mix of stagflation and fiscal strain kept investors from buying French paper, though the front end is less exposed to budget risk than the long end and still tracks ECB pricing.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.55–3.75%, led by ECB pricing; a failed budget vote would widen spreads more at long maturities than here.
fr2y.watch: Euro flash CPI Nov 4, the budget vote around Nov 3 and the Nov 5 strike.

fr5y.note: Up a few bp while Bunds rallied; the spread to Germany widened after weak French data.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT underperformed as an unexpected 0.1% Q3 contraction and 3.8% inflation revived worries about France's debt path, with public debt near 120% of GDP and the 2027 budget still stuck in parliament. Investors sold French debt and bought Bunds, the opposite of Thursday when the ECB's soft hold helped OATs.
fr5y.outlook: Bias for a wider spread to Bunds into the budget vote and Fitch's negative outlook; outright direction follows euro CPI and the ECB.
fr5y.watch: The budget vote around Nov 3, euro CPI Nov 4 and the Nov 5 OAT auction.

fr10y.note: Up about 2bp to near 4.98%; spread to Bunds widened about 4bp to roughly 165bp vs a 177bp peak on Oct 22.
fr10y.why: French yields jumped after GDP fell 0.1% in Q3 against a 0.1% gain expected and inflation rose to 3.8%, above the 3.6% forecast, with the 10-year near 4.98% at one point. The spread over Bunds widened as money moved into Germany. After the close, Fitch cut France's outlook to negative, saying political fragmentation is undermining debt stabilisation and seeing debt near 124% of GDP by 2028.
fr10y.outlook: Spread range 155–175bp with a widening bias after Fitch. A failed budget vote or political crisis would push it back toward 175bp and the 10-year above 5%; budget progress could narrow it to 155bp.
fr10y.watch: Market reaction to Fitch on Nov 2, the budget vote around Nov 3, the Nov 5 auction and strike, and S&P Nov 27.

fr30y.note: Near 5.46%, little changed; the long-end spread to Germany stays near 180bp.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT held near its highs because the long end carries most of France's fiscal risk premium, and Friday's data made it worse: a Q3 contraction and 3.8% inflation point to stagflation, which hurts both the deficit and real returns. Fitch's negative outlook came after the close and has not yet been priced, and a national strike is planned for Nov 5.
fr30y.outlook: Range 5.35–5.60% with an upside bias after Fitch and into the Nov 5 long-term auction; a smooth budget vote would ease it toward 5.35%.
fr30y.watch: The budget vote around Nov 3, the Nov 5 auction and strike, and S&P Nov 27.

watch: Next: OPEC+ Nov 1, ISM manufacturing and the market reaction to Fitch Nov 2, the US midterms and French budget vote Nov 3, euro flash CPI, the US refunding and EIA stocks Nov 4, the BoE and OAT auction Nov 5, and payrolls Nov 6.
sources: Dow Jones via MarketScreener (US and euro bonds)
